chunk_findings.detail: The cache key is built from the unresolved `gdef.command`, while the command that actually runs is produced later by `WK.resolve(...)`. If `WK.resolve` expands or changes the command (for example, a gate command containing `auto` becomes `-n 1` in one environment and `-n 8` in another, or suite-holding changes the resolved command/timeout), two runs with different effective commands get the same `rc_key`. A stored result from the first run can therefore be returned for the second run without executing the different command, despite the comment claiming the hit is for the same command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/runner.py:302

chunk_findings.detail: A dirty submodule is removed from the cache key instead of being represented. `git diff HEAD --name-only` reports a modified submodule as a path, but the code then checks `path.is_file()` and, because the path is a directory, executes `entries.pop(rel, None)` without adding any worktree entry. Thus the parent HEAD gitlink entry is erased and the submodule commit is not included in `code_key`. Given a HEAD that contains submodule `lib` at commit `X`, a run with `lib` checked out at commit `Y` can store a passed result; a later run with `lib` checked out at a different commit `Z` computes the same code key because `lib` is absent from the hashed rows, so the cache serves the old passed result even though the tree differs.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_code_entries

chunk_findings.detail: The key does not include the version of the resolved gate command, only the command string. For example, with the same tree, the same command `"pytest"`, no lockfile change, and no `resultcache.env_vars` entry capturing the tool version or `PATH`, upgrading the global `pytest` executable from 7.x to 8.x leaves `_python()`, `sys.platform`, `_env()`, `tree`, and `command` unchanged. `key()` therefore returns the previous key, and a cached passed result from the old tool version is served for the new tool version.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:key

chunk_findings.detail: An unreadable lockfile is silently omitted rather than causing a cache miss. If `Path(cwd)/name` exists but `p.read_text(...)` raises `PermissionError` or another `OSError`, the `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` skips the append entirely, so the lockfile contributes no part to the digest. With `uv.lock` present but unreadable by the cache process, two runs with different lockfile contents can produce the same key, allowing the second run to hit the first run's passed entry even though the dependency lock file changed and was not read back whole.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_env

chunk_findings.detail: For changed or untracked files, the code stores only `f"worktree {blob}"`, dropping the file mode. Clean HEAD entries include mode, but worktree entries do not. Given an untracked file `run.sh` with identical contents but mode `755` in one run and mode `644` in another, `_code_entries` produces the same entry and `code_key` is identical. If the gate command invokes `./run.sh`, the first run may pass while the second would fail because the file is not executable, but the cache reuses the passed result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_code_entries

chunk_findings.detail: `resultcache.enabled` is added with `new = 'true'`, so an upgrade turns the cache on for existing projects, while the documented key (`ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md:117`) only hashes tracked files, the gate, the command string, the Python version, dependency lock files, and `[resultcache].env_vars` (default `[]`). Given a project with no dependency lock files and a `ci` gate whose command is `pytest`, run it once in an environment with pytest 7.4 and it passes; the result is cached. Then change only the environment/tool version, e.g. `pip install --upgrade pytest` to 8.0 or switch `PATH` to another virtualenv where the tests fail. The tracked files, gate name, command string, Python version, lock files, and `env_vars` are unchanged, so the second run is served `passed` from cache. This reports a failed gate as passed; the key must include the resolved interpreter/tool version (or full environment), or the feature must not default to enabled.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.resultcache.enabled.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The `git` helper is not hermetic: it copies the ambient environment and only overrides author/committer identity. If a developer’s global Git config enables signing (`commit.gpgsign=true`) or hooks (`core.hooksPath`), the `git commit -q -m init` calls in `project()` and `commit()` can fail, causing every test that creates a repository to error. For example, with a global config containing `commit.gpgsign=true` and no usable signing key, `git(repo, "commit", ...)` raises `CalledProcessError`. The helper should isolate Git config (e.g. `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=os.devnull`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=os.devnull`) or pass `--no-gpg-sign --no-verify`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_result_cache.py:18-28

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_worktree_shares_the_projects_cache` only asserts that `RC.entry_path(repo, "k").parent == RC.entry_path(wt, "k").parent`. That proves the worktree resolves to the same cache directory, but it does not prove cache results are shared. If `RC.key` includes the absolute worktree path (or the worktree’s branch), the repo and linked worktree will produce different keys for the same tree, so a result stored from the repo will never be looked up from the worktree; the test still passes because both `entry_path` calls have the same parent directory.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_result_cache.py:192-196

chunk_findings.detail: The gate commands embed `tmp_path` unquoted into shell redirection (`echo ran >> {tmp_path}/...`). If pytest’s temporary directory path contains spaces (common on Windows user profiles, or on POSIX systems with a spaced `TMPDIR`), the shell splits the redirection target. For example, with `tmp_path=/tmp/pytest 123/test`, the command becomes `echo ran >> /tmp/pytest 123/test/count.txt`, which redirects to `/tmp/pytest` and then tries to execute `123/test/count.txt`, so the gate command fails or writes the wrong file and the test fails. The paths should be shell-quoted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_result_cache.py:252,272

chunk_findings.detail: The test starts a thread that is expected to acquire the queued lock and append `"agent-y"` to `got`, then calls `t.join(10)`, but it never asserts `got` or that the thread finished. If the lock release path fails to wake the queued holder, or the thread times out/raises after creating the ticket, the ticket note can still contain `class: integrator` and the final assertion passes even though the queued hold never acquired the lock. For example, if `SL.hold` writes the queued ticket with the class but does not release the lock to the waiting thread, this test still succeeds.

chunk_findings.detail: The cache key and lookup omit the effective gate timeout. The run later uses `timeout_s = WK.timeout_for(gdef.timeout_s, auto, cfg)`, but `RC.key(gdef.id, gdef.command, cwd, conf)` and `RC.lookup(cwd, rc_key, conf)` are given only the gate id, command, cwd, and config. Given a gate whose command passes in 10 seconds with `gdef.timeout_s=60`, the passed outcome is stored. If the same gate id/command/tree/environment is then run with `gdef.timeout_s=5`, the computed `rc_key` is unchanged, the cache hit returns `passed`, and the gate wrongly reports success even though the command would be killed at 5 seconds and should fail or be unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/runner.py:300

chunk_findings.detail: The new default for `resultcache.env_vars` is `[]`, and `ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md` says the cache key includes only the variables named by `[resultcache].env_vars`. With `resultcache.enabled` defaulting to true, this makes the gate result cache key environment-invariant by default. Example: a `ci` gate runs `pytest tests/test_stage.py`, and that test asserts `os.environ["DDFLOW_STAGE"] == "prod"`. Run 1 with `DDFLOW_STAGE=prod` passes and is cached. Run 2 on the same tracked tree, same command, same Python version and dependency lock files, but with `DDFLOW_STAGE=dev`, computes the same cache key because `env_vars` is empty, so the cached `passed` result is returned even though the correct outcome is `failed`. The same class of miss applies to inherited toolchain variables such as `PATH`, `PYTHONPATH`, or `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so different tool versions can also hit the cache. This contradicts the documented “same environment” requirement and can serve an incorrect passed result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.resultcache.env_vars.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The added test treats two different base trees as the same tree whenever their dirty-tree suffix/content id matches. The events use `tree_sha` values `aaaaaaa1+st:abc123` and `bbbbbbb2+st:abc123`, so the base tree SHA part differs (`aaaaaaa1` vs `bbbbbbb2`), but the test asserts `rep["classes"]["unplaced"]["runs"] == 0` and one `rerun_same_tree_other_item` run. That means suite-waste placement, and any cache key derived from it, can place or reuse a gate result for a run on a different tree. For example, a passed result produced for item A on tree `aaaaaaa1` with stash/content `abc123` could be counted as avoidable for item B on tree `bbbbbbb2` with the same stash/content, even though the underlying tree changed. A dirty-tree cache/placement key must include both the base tree and the dirty content id, not just the `+st:` content id.

chunk_findings.detail: `enabled` defaults to `True`, so an upgrade turns the result cache on for projects that have not configured `[resultcache].env_vars`. The same knob documentation says the key includes Python, lock files, probe commands, command string, and tree, while `env_vars` defaults to `[]`; arbitrary environment variables that change test behavior are therefore not part of the key. Concrete failure: a Python project has `ci.command = "pytest"` and tests that pass only when `PYTHONHASHSEED=0` but fail when it is unset or another value. The first run is executed with `PYTHONHASHSEED=0`, passes, and is cached. A later run on the same tree with `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` (or unset) returns the cached `passed` result and records the gate as passed without running it, because `PYTHONHASHSEED` is not in `env_vars` and the cache is enabled by default. The added `probe_commands` default hashes tool versions, not environment variables, so the previously confirmed default-enabled false-hit concern still holds.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/resultcache.py:ResultCacheConfig.enabled

chunk_findings.detail: `_probe` is memoized by the command string only, and `_env` never passes the project `cwd` or the current environment to it. Given `cfg.resultcache.probe_commands = ["./venv/bin/pytest --version"]` (or any probe whose output depends on `PATH`/`cwd`) and no `resultcache.env_vars` entry, the first call in a ddflow process caches the version seen in the process’s current `PATH`/`cwd`. A later run in the same process for a linked worktree, or after activating a different virtualenv, calls `_env` with a different `cwd`/environment, but `_probe` returns the stale digest; `key()` therefore returns the old key and `lookup()` can serve a cached `passed` result even though the gate command now resolves to a different tool version. A transient probe timeout is also cached as `unavailable`, hiding later environment changes. The probe component must be keyed by the resolved execution environment/cwd or not cached.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_probe

chunk_findings.detail: The submodule branch records only `git rev-parse HEAD` inside the submodule directory; it never hashes the submodule’s worktree files. If a parent tree contains submodule `lib` at commit `X`, two runs with different dirty modifications inside `lib` but with `lib` still at HEAD `X` produce the same `code_key`: the entry is either the unchanged HEAD gitlink or, when the parent diff lists the dirty submodule, the same `submodule X` entry. A cached `passed` result from one dirty submodule state can therefore be served for another dirty state whose tests would fail. Additionally, when the submodule directory is not itself a git repository (for example, uninitialized), `G.run(path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")` searches upward and records the parent HEAD as the submodule commit, which is wrong. The submodule worktree state must be represented, or the key must miss.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_code_entries

chunk_findings.detail: `path.exists()` follows symlinks, so a broken symlink is treated as a missing path. Git reports a broken symlink as an untracked or changed path, but `_code_entries` pops/omits it, making the code key identical to a tree where that path does not exist. Example: a prior run with `run.sh` absent passes and is cached; a later run with `run.sh` as a broken symlink and gate command `test ! -L run.sh` would fail, but the cache key is the same and the cached pass is served. The code should use `os.path.lexists`/`lstat` and represent the symlink blob/mode.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_code_entries

chunk_findings.detail: The upgrade still adds `resultcache.enabled` with `new = 'true'`, so existing projects get the cache turned on, while the help topic added in this change (`ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md:117`) still defines the cache key as only tracked files minus `.ddflow/`/docs, the gate, the command string, the Python version, dependency lock files, and `[resultcache].env_vars` (default `[]`). That documented key has no component for the resolved executable/tool version or PATH. Given a project with no dependency lock file and a `ci` gate command `pytest`, a first run under pytest 7.4 can store a passed entry; after upgrading the global `pytest` to 8.x, the tree, command string, Python version, lock fingerprint, and default `env_vars` are unchanged, so a rerun computes the same key and is recorded as passed from cache even if the new pytest fails. This is the previously confirmed finding 6/3 still standing: the knob remains default-on and the documented key still omits the tool version.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.resultcache.enabled.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The test only compares the key after moving the submodule to a different commit with the key from the clean HEAD. Under the previously confirmed bug where a dirty submodule path is popped from the key and no worktree entry is added, the key already changes relative to the clean HEAD because the HEAD gitlink entry is simply missing, so this test can pass even though two different dirty submodule commits still collide. It also does not assert that `before` is non-`None`. To fail the unfixed code it should capture the dirty key at one submodule commit, move the submodule to another commit, and assert the key changes again (or otherwise prove the submodule commit is part of the key).
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_result_cache.py:test_a_submodule_at_another_commit_misses

chunk_findings.detail: The test only asserts that `RC.lookup(...)` misses for bad outcomes; it never checks that `store` did not write an entry. If `store` writes `unavailable`, `partial`, `skipped`, empty, or unknown outcomes but `lookup` merely filters them out, this test passes while the cache still contains non-pass/fail entries, contrary to the stated invariant that only passed and failed results are cached. It should assert that `RC.entry_path(repo, k)` does not exist after each bad store.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_result_cache.py:test_unavailable_partial_and_unknown_outcomes_are_never_stored

chunk_findings.detail: The test returns early when `os.access(repo / "uv.lock", os.R_OK)` is true after `chmod(0)`. Running as root, or with ACLs/capabilities that make a mode-0 file readable, makes `os.access` true, so the test never calls `key(repo)` and passes even if the unfixed code silently omits unreadable lockfiles. The test should force the read failure (for example, by monkeypatching the lockfile reader to raise `OSError`) rather than skipping the assertion in readable-as-root environments.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_result_cache.py:test_an_unreadable_lock_file_means_no_key

chunk_findings.detail: The test still does not prove that the queued hold completed: it calls `t.join(10)` but ignores the return value and never checks `t.is_alive()`. If `SL.hold` appends `"agent-y"` and then blocks or raises only in cleanup/`__exit__`, `got == ["agent-y"]` and the ticket-note assertions can still pass while the thread is alive and the lock was not released. The previous round’s concern that the thread’s completion is not asserted is therefore not fully answered.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_queue_priority.py::test_a_block_can_queue_its_holds_as_a_class

chunk_findings.detail: The cache key and lookup omit the effective gate timeout. The run later uses `timeout_s = WK.timeout_for(gdef.timeout_s, auto, cfg)`, but `RC.key(gdef.id, gdef.command, cwd, conf)` and `RC.lookup(cwd, rc_key, conf)` are given only the gate id, command, cwd, and config. Given a gate whose command passes in 10 seconds with `gdef.timeout_s=60`, the passed outcome is stored. If the same gate id/command/tree/environment is then run with `gdef.timeout_s=5`, the computed `rc_key` is unchanged, the cache hit returns `passed`, and the gate wrongly reports success even though the command would be killed at 5 seconds and should fail or be unavailable.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/runner.py:300

chunk_findings.detail: The new default for `resultcache.env_vars` is `[]`, and `ddflow/templates/prompts/help/parallel.md` says the cache key includes only the variables named by `[resultcache].env_vars`. With `resultcache.enabled` defaulting to true, this makes the gate result cache key environment-invariant by default. Example: a `ci` gate runs `pytest tests/test_stage.py`, and that test asserts `os.environ["DDFLOW_STAGE"] == "prod"`. Run 1 with `DDFLOW_STAGE=prod` passes and is cached. Run 2 on the same tracked tree, same command, same Python version and dependency lock files, but with `DDFLOW_STAGE=dev`, computes the same cache key because `env_vars` is empty, so the cached `passed` result is returned even though the correct outcome is `failed`. The same class of miss applies to inherited toolchain variables such as `PATH`, `PYTHONPATH`, or `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, so different tool versions can also hit the cache. This contradicts the documented “same environment” requirement and can serve an incorrect passed result.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.resultcache.env_vars.toml:4

chunk_findings.detail: The added test treats two different base trees as the same tree whenever their dirty-tree suffix/content id matches. The events use `tree_sha` values `aaaaaaa1+st:abc123` and `bbbbbbb2+st:abc123`, so the base tree SHA part differs (`aaaaaaa1` vs `bbbbbbb2`), but the test asserts `rep["classes"]["unplaced"]["runs"] == 0` and one `rerun_same_tree_other_item` run. That means suite-waste placement, and any cache key derived from it, can place or reuse a gate result for a run on a different tree. For example, a passed result produced for item A on tree `aaaaaaa1` with stash/content `abc123` could be counted as avoidable for item B on tree `bbbbbbb2` with the same stash/content, even though the underlying tree changed. A dirty-tree cache/placement key must include both the base tree and the dirty content id, not just the `+st:` content id.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_suite_waste.py:276

chunk_findings.detail: The new cache key includes only the declared `gdef.timeout_s`, but the runner’s actual timeout is later computed as `WK.timeout_for(gdef.timeout_s, auto, cfg)`. The effective timeout is still not fully represented in the key: `auto` is an input to the effective timeout but is not included in `RC.key(...)`. Given the same tracked tree, gate id, command, config, and declared timeout, but a run where `auto` causes `WK.timeout_for` to choose a shorter effective limit, `RC.key` produces the same hash as a prior longer-timeout pass. The cache then returns the prior `passed` outcome even though the current run would have timed out or failed under the effective limit. This is the same effective-timeout defect from the earlier confirmed finding, only partially fixed: changes to the declared timeout are now distinguished, but changes to the effective timeout caused by `auto` are not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/gates/runner.py:300

chunk_findings.detail: `_probe` is decorated with `@functools.cache`, so the result of a probe command is cached by the command string alone. The probe result nevertheless depends on the current working directory and process environment (`PATH`, virtualenv, project-local tool shims, etc.), none of which are part of the cache key. Given `resultcache.probe_commands = ["pytest --version"]`, if the first `key()` call in a ddflow process runs when `pytest` resolves to version 8.0, `_probe("pytest --version")` caches the digest of 8.0. A later `key()` call in the same process for another project/worktree, or after the environment has changed to a different venv where `pytest` is 9.0, still receives the cached 8.0 digest. The cache key therefore does not change when the effective tool version changes, so a previously stored `passed` entry can be reused for a run that would now fail because of the tool upgrade. This directly undermines the stated tool-version part of the key.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_probe

chunk_findings.detail: The new branch `if path.is_dir():  # a submodule` treats every directory in `changed`/`untracked` as a submodule. If a plain untracked directory reaches this loop, `G.run(path, "rev-parse", "HEAD")` succeeds by resolving the enclosing repository and records the superproject HEAD as the directory’s identity. For example, add a new untracked directory `tests_new/` containing `test_stage.py`; if the untracked set reports the collapsed directory (`?? tests_new/`, as default `git status --porcelain` can do), the first run caches a pass with entry `tests_new=submodule <head>`. A later edit to `tests_new/test_stage.py` that makes the test fail still reports the same collapsed directory, so the key is unchanged and the cached pass is reused. This violates the acceptance requirement that changing one code file misses; the code should verify that the path is actually a submodule or expand untracked directories into their contained files.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/resultcache.py:_entries

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not actually move the superproject’s tracked submodule pointer. After `submodule add` and the commit, `before = key(repo)` fingerprints a gitlink at the original `lib` commit. The later `commit(lib, ...)` plus `git -C repo/lib pull ...` changes only the submodule checkout, leaving the superproject’s tracked tree with the same gitlink and the same tree SHA; it merely makes the superproject dirty with an unstaged submodule change. Thus, if `RC.key` is built from the tracked tree as specified, the second `key(repo)` returns `before` and the assertion fails; if it returns a different key because it also fingerprints dirty submodule state, the test is passing on a dirty-tree case rather than the required “submodule at another commit” case. To exercise the stated miss, the test must record the new submodule commit in the superproject, e.g. `git(repo, "add", "lib")` and `git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "bump lib")` before computing the second key.
